intro: Slack for computer systems analysts on Mac is mostly a coordination tool. You use it to collect requirements, track change requests, and hand off decisions between business managers and the IT team. This guide covers the Mac setup, the Slack features that fit this job, and where Lazur helps while you work. Lazur adds voice help on top of Slack. It does not replace Slack, and it does not click for you.
tldr: Give each project its own channel. Keep decisions in threads so they stay easy to search later.
Track requirements in Slack Lists. Pro and Business+ lists hold up to 1,000 items each.
Build intake and handoff steps with workflows from Agents & tools > Workflows. Each workflow caps at 100 steps.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where a setting is. Lazur draws a circle around it on your screen.
Lazur guides you one click at a time. You do the clicking, and you read the text before you press Send.

blocks.text: Computer systems analysts sit between the business and the IT department. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics describes them as a liaison between management and IT. They explain complex technical issues so both sides understand them. A lot of the job is conversation, and a lot of that conversation is follow-up. Slack is often where that conversation happens. This guide shows how to set up Slack for Mac for that work. Everything here works without Lazur. Lazur only adds voice help on top.
What the job asks for, and where Slack fits

The Bureau of Labor Statistics lists the core duties. Analysts meet with managers to work out how IT systems fit the organization's work. They analyze the costs and benefits of systems and upgrades. They design new systems, oversee installation, test systems, and write manuals and train end users. Each duty creates messages, files, and decisions. Slack holds the messages. Lists and workflows hold the tasks and the intake forms. The mapping below is my suggestion. No Slack or BLS source describes how analysts use Slack day to day.

items: Meet managers to see how systems fit their work: use a channel per business unit, plus a standing thread for open questions.
Analyze costs and benefits: keep the numbers in a thread or a Slack List, so the decision has a record.
Design and test systems: track test cases and defects as list items, each with an owner and a due date.
Write manuals and train users: pin the final version to the channel so people stop asking for it.
Handle change requests: send them through a workflow form, so every request arrives with the same fields.

blocks.text: Set up Slack for Mac for requirements work

Start with the version. Slack's Mac release notes list build 4.53.280, dated November 3, 2026, as a security update. That is the newest build I could confirm on the page while writing this guide. Open the Slack menu and check your version against it. If you run an older build, update before you rely on Lists or workflows. Menus and labels have changed in recent builds.

The automation area of the sidebar has a new name. Slack's developer changelog describes a renamed and revamped Agents & Tools tab, with a landing page to help users find popular agents. Some help articles still say Tools or More. Older university guides say Automations. If you cannot find the entry, look for those names.

blocks.title: Pin the two channels you check first
blocks.text: Pin the channels you open every morning to the top of the sidebar. Archive finished projects, so the sidebar shows only live work.
Name channels so search finds them

Use one channel per project, with a short prefix. A name such as proj-claims-portal is easy to find with ⌘K. Slack channel names are lowercase, and they use hyphens instead of spaces. Make a channel public when the whole team needs it. Make it private when the content is sensitive, such as a vendor price comparison or a security finding. For the setup steps, read [how to create a channel in Slack on Mac](/how-to/create-a-channel-in-slack).
Track requirements with Slack Lists

Slack Lists turn a requirements backlog into rows you can sort and assign. To start one on Mac, go to Home > Files, click the plus button, and choose List. You can also go to Home > Files > Lists > See all to pick a template. New lists come with four default fields: Completion, Name, Assignee, and Due Date. Add the fields your project needs on top of those. If you already keep requirements in a spreadsheet, choose New > Import a CSV and load the file.

blocks.caption: List limits, from Slack's help article Use lists in Slack

blocks.text: Plan for the cap early. Keep one list per release or per system, not one list for the whole company. When a list reaches its limit, Slack archives the oldest items for you. Treat that as a warning, not a cleanup. Frontline Members cannot create lists. If a teammate sees no List option, check their role with your admin.
Build intake forms and handoffs with workflows

Workflows handle the repeated work. A form collects a change request, a reviewer gets a message, and the answers land in the right channel. To start from a template, open Agents & tools > Workflows > Templates. For a standard template, click Set Up and follow the prompts. Advanced templates open in Workflow Builder so you can edit the steps. Slack's help article says Advanced templates need a paid plan.

By default, Full Members can create workflows, and members and guests can use them. If you cannot create one, your admin may have changed that default. Ask before you plan a process that depends on a workflow you cannot build.

items: Open Agents & tools > Workflows > Templates, then pick a standard template that asks for a request.
Click Set Up and follow the prompts. Standard templates publish when you finish.
Edit the questions so they match your intake: system, business reason, requested date, and expected impact.
Test the form with a colleague in a private channel before the wider team sees it.

blocks.title: Watch the 100-step cap
blocks.text: A workflow can hold up to 100 steps. A long approval chain can reach that limit sooner than you expect. Split the process into two workflows, one for intake and one for review.
Keep decisions searchable in threads

A decision made in the main channel scrolls out of view quickly in a busy channel. Put each question in a thread and keep the answer there. Pin the final decision, so anyone can find it in one click. Save messages you need later instead of copying them into a notes file. Copies drift, and the original message does not. Read [how to reply in a thread in Slack on Mac](/how-to/reply-in-a-thread-in-slack), [how to pin a message in Slack on Mac](/how-to/pin-a-message-in-slack), and [how to save a message for later in Slack on Mac](/how-to/save-a-message-for-later-in-slack).
Use the keyboard to jump, search, and find unreads

Press ⌘K to open the quick switcher. Type part of a channel or person name, then press Return. That is faster than scrolling the sidebar when you juggle several projects. Press ⇧ Return to start a new line in a message without sending it. To find something in one channel, search inside that conversation first, since the results are narrower.

To catch up after a meeting, open the Unreads view. Mark a message unread when you need to come back to it, and it stays on your list. Check the shortcuts list in Slack before you memorize a set, because menus change between builds. Start with [how to jump to a conversation in Slack on Mac](/how-to/jump-to-a-conversation-in-slack) and [how to show the keyboard shortcuts in Slack on Mac](/how-to/show-the-keyboard-shortcuts-list-in-slack).
Cut notification noise during requirements work

Slack's 2024 Workforce Index surveyed 10,045 workers in six countries. It found that desk workers spend about a third of their day on tasks they consider low-value. That figure is self-reported and rounded, so treat it as a signal. The same report says 75% of knowledge workers use more apps than they did five years ago.

Protect your long analysis blocks. Pause notifications before a requirements session, then set a schedule for the daily check. Mute busy channels, and keep only your project channel loud. If alerts stop arriving, work through the notification fixes before you blame the app. See [how to pause notifications in Slack on Mac](/how-to/pause-notifications-in-slack), [how to mute a channel in Slack on Mac](/how-to/mute-a-channel-in-slack), and [how to fix Slack notifications on Mac](/how-to/fix-missing-notifications-in-slack).
Ask Lazur about Slack by voice

Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac that lives in the notch. Hold ⌥ ⌘, which means Option and Command together, and ask your question out loud. Lazur looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut. Then it answers out loud. It works in any app, so it can read the Slack window you have open. It is not a Slack plugin or add-in. Slack stays the app you use, and Lazur sits alongside it on your Mac.

Ask where something is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it. Ask how to do something, and Lazur guides you one click at a time. It waits for each click before it gives the next step. Lazur does not click for you. That matters in Slack, where one click can post a message to a whole channel.
Dictate replies with fn

Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Use it for long thread replies, meeting notes, and test summaries. Snippets, a personal dictionary, and clipboard slots handle the phrases you repeat, such as your standard status line. Read the text before you press Send. Dictation is quick, and it can mishear a system name.
Worked example: a change request from intake to close

Here is one example with invented names. A sales manager fills in the change request form in your intake workflow. The form asks for the system, the business reason, the requested date, and the expected impact. The answers post into the review thread. You open your Slack List and add a row for the request. You set the Assignee and Due Date fields, then reply in the thread with your open questions.

Next, you ask Lazur to draft the reply text. You edit the draft, then hold fn to dictate the last sentence. When the reviewer approves, you pin the decision in the thread. You move the row to done in the Completion field. Every step stayed in Slack. Lazur helped with wording and menu steps. It never sent anything for you.
Mistakes analysts make in Slack

items: Keeping requirements in direct messages. Move them to a channel or a List, so the team can see them.
Answering in the main channel. Replies there bury the decision. Put answers in a thread instead.
Building one List for everything. A List on Pro or Business+ holds 1,000 items, then archives the oldest.
Forgetting the step cap. A workflow stops at 100 steps, so split long processes early.
Trusting an old menu path. Labels have changed in recent builds, so check your version first.
Sending dictated text unread. Dictation is fast, and it can get a technical term wrong.

blocks.text: What Lazur does and does not do in Slack

Lazur guides, points, explains, answers out loud, drafts and types text. It does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app, Slack included. It runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available.

Privacy matters when your work includes client data. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Check your company policy before you share sensitive channels with any AI tool.
Price and trial

Lazur starts with a Pro trial, and the trial needs no credit card. The clock starts the first time you open the app. Dictation is unlimited on both paid plans. The Pro and Power plans differ in how many AI actions they include, and each one can be billed monthly or annually. Check the [pricing page](/pricing) for the current amounts before you decide.
Next steps for this week

items: Check that your Slack for Mac build is 4.53.280 or newer, and update if it is not.
Create one channel for each active project, and pin the two you check first.
Build one List for your open requirements, or import a CSV if you already have one.
Set up one intake workflow for change requests, and test it in a private channel first.
[Download Lazur](/download), then hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask where the Lists entry is.

faq.question: Is there a separate Slack app for computer systems analysts on Mac?
faq.answer: No. Analysts use the standard Slack for Mac app. The features that help most are channels, Slack Lists, workflows, threads, and notification controls. Your workspace admin decides which features your plan includes, so check with them first.

faq.question: Which Slack features need a paid plan?
faq.answer: Slack's help article says Advanced workflow templates need a paid plan. Lists also depend on your plan, and Frontline Members cannot create lists. Slack's help article does not spell out what free teams get, so confirm with your admin or Slack's pricing page.

faq.question: How many items can one Slack List hold?
faq.answer: On Pro and Business+ plans, a list holds up to 1,000 items and subtasks. Enterprise Grid allows 5,000. When a list reaches its limit, the oldest items are archived automatically.

faq.question: How many steps can a Slack workflow have?
faq.answer: Slack's FAQ says you can add up to 100 steps to a workflow. If a process is longer, split it into two workflows. Each one stays easier to read and easier to test.

faq.question: Does Lazur send Slack messages for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur drafts text, and it can dictate text at your cursor while you hold fn. You read the text and press Send yourself. Lazur does not click buttons or operate other apps for you.

faq.question: Is Lazur a Slack plugin or add-in?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is a voice assistant for the Mac. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app, Slack included. It works in any window you open, so you can ask about Slack while you use it.

faq.question: What happens to my voice and screen when I use Lazur?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.

faq.question: Which Macs does Lazur run on?
faq.answer: Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, but it is not available yet.
